zeroRateInterrogation.verdict: non-zero on the planted population; 9/9 agree (store-only reachable: false) on the unplanted second population
zeroRateInterrogation.claimNotMade: This run does NOT establish that the source-resolved and store-derived positions always agree, nor that they disagree on real repositories. It establishes what happened on this 10-row comparable sample, lists every non-comparable row with its reason, and separates the planted rows from the ones the real indexer wrote.
zeroRateInterrogation.whyARateIsNotTheGate: A rate is a description of one population. What makes the cross-check trustworthy is that a difference CANNOT be absorbed: bucket reachability is asserted on real rows here (a planted disagree and a planted store-only row must both be detected) and again under the fixture double in script/m24/verify-call-hierarchy.ts G13, with 13 mutation legs planting defects in the cross-check and the counts.
zeroRateInterrogation.bucketReachabilityProvenHere: planted disagree >= 1, planted store-only >= 1, planted source-only >= 1 — asserted above

zeroRateInterrogation.coverageNotClaimed: one purpose-built fixture; per-language coverage on real repositories is NOT measured and NOT claimed

secondPopulation.why: a disagreement class that exists only under a hand-written store state is not evidence that the class OCCURS. This population is indexed by the real indexer with NOTHING planted.

storeOnlyUnplantedAbsence.why: no unplanted row in either population carries a call-site line the caller's own text does not show. Every unplanted row's stored line names an invocation the text contains. measurement.zeroDifferenceRateNote: A zero disagreement rate would NOT mean the two sources always agree: it would more likely mean the compared population is too small or too uniform. This run measured a NON-ZERO disagreement count and lists every row; the denominator is on every figure so a reader can judge the population rather than trust the rate.

lawsAsserted: Law 1: the five buckets partition every measured row (a rate over a moving denominator is not a measurement)

Law 2: ROW-WISE, on every stored row both this script and the component classified, the two verdicts are identical, and a non-agreeing row was declared by the component. The overlap is required to be non-empty and to be more than one row, so the law cannot pass vacuously. §13.4 is asserted on every response driven here

Law 2 does NOT compare aggregate totals: this script measures every stored row while the component reads only what the engine hands it for the roots driven, and the component dedupes callers. A totals comparison would conflate a population difference with a disagreement.
limitations: one fixture project; per-language coverage on real repositories is NOT measured and NOT claimed

the resolver is the component's own (imported, not re-implemented) because a second implementation would be a second source of truth - the thing D4 exists to end; the CLASSIFICATION here is written independently so the two verdicts are comparable
the engine's depth is obtained by traversal; a row no traversal reached is reported as depth 0 (unstated) rather than assumed direct
the store-only bucket counts rows where the scan cannot see the invocation; attributing such a row to a macro/template/dynamic dispatch is an INFERENCE from the store and the text, not a diagnosis
